## Context / Problem

Nine real scanner integration tests skip when binaries are absent at `tests/unit/test_code_review_conflict_markers.py:97-158`, `test_code_review_public_exposure.py:109-151`, and `test_code_review_ws5.py:347-399`. Verified installs neither scanner although `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:43-71` makes them runtime prerequisites.

## Approach

Create a checked-in scanner lock manifest that explicitly targets `linux/amd64` and is consumed by both the review-bot image and CI provisioning. Model the two installation mechanisms separately:

- The Gitleaks manifest entry owns its pinned version, published per-release Linux/amd64 asset URL, and that tarball’s SHA-256. The installer must verify the digest before extraction.
- The Semgrep manifest entry owns its pinned version and points to a committed, fully resolved Linux/amd64 requirements lock. The lock records every pip distribution hash needed for Semgrep; the installer uses `pip install --require-hashes` so it never treats Semgrep as a fictional single downloadable artifact.

Add one provisioning helper that validates the manifest’s platform against its Docker build target or CI runner before installing either scanner. The Dockerfile and explicit Make target call that helper rather than reimplementing versions or integrity checks. Configure the reusable lane on a Linux x64 runner and have it self-check the same manifest platform before provisioning, so deployment and Verified consume the same entries.

This deliberately supersedes the current dynamic-Gitleaks/latest and unpinned-Semgrep choices. Gitleaks provides stable per-release assets plus published checksums; the reproducibility and integrity benefit now outweighs the earlier pinned-version-404 concern. Document the manifest as the sole update point and the scanner-bump procedure in `docs/security.md`.

Do not build Docker, install OpenGrep, or add this target to normal `make lint`/default local tests.

## Scope

- platform-aware scanner manifest, Semgrep hash-lock file, and review-bot Dockerfile
- shared provisioning helper and explicit Make target
- scanner integration tests
- reusable mirror/Gerrit workflow and Verified parity guard
- `docs/security.md` scanner-lock ownership and update procedure

## Testing

Exercise a Linux/amd64 platform mismatch, missing Gitleaks, a bad Gitleaks SHA-256, a missing or bad Semgrep requirement hash, and wrong scanner versions. Prove the valid hash-locked Semgrep rule and valid Gitleaks secret/SARIF cases pass all nine real integration contracts. Exercise workflow wiring and `vote.needs` parity structurally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The checked-in scanner manifest names `linux/amd64`; the Docker build path and the reusable CI lane validate and consume that same platform entry before provisioning.
- [ ] The Gitleaks entry pins one published Linux/amd64 release asset URL, version, and SHA-256; a bad digest or wrong version fails before the focused contracts run.
- [ ] The Semgrep entry pins its version through a fully resolved requirements lock containing every required distribution hash; provisioning uses `pip --require-hashes`, and a missing or bad lock hash fails before the focused contracts run.
- [ ] The shared installer is the only deployment/CI provisioner for these scanner pins; `docs/security.md` identifies its manifest and the version-bump procedure.
- [ ] The explicit native-binary target fails for a platform mismatch or missing scanner and passes the nine real Semgrep/Gitleaks integration contracts with valid pinned inputs.
- [ ] One parallel reusable lane serves mirror CI and exact Gerrit patchsets and is required by the Verified vote.
- [ ] OpenGrep, Docker-image builds, normal `make lint`, and default local tests remain outside scope.
- [ ] The lane's expected cold-run cost is documented as approximately 1.5-3 runner-minutes without extending the existing 22-23 minute critical path when capacity is available.
